D.t: John Hickenlooper leads by 18.3 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 519,366 votes; a one point swing is about 14,159 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +9.6 and D +26.7. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 217,910 votes; Boulder, a projected net 112,626 votes; Arapahoe, a projected net 91,750 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +4.4, 11.9% of the vote; Douglas, R +3.1, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +3.4, 2.7% of the vote; Garfield, D +9.6, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, John Hickenlooper runs furthest behind in Weld, Mesa, Douglas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 55 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.08 points; Large counties, 79% of voters, 61 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.93 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points.
The forecast's worst groups for John Hickenlooper: Immigration voters 28 to 70, Small counties 46 to 52, Midsize counties 49 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.1M cash against $28K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
